name: Halversen & Co. Detach Hood (Crofton Wool)
description:
A standalone detachable hood in dense Crofton wool-analog — a genetic-mill fiber with the warmth of merino and the water-shedding of oilcloth. Colorway is a deep teal-brown heather with visible slub texture. The hood attaches via a concealed magnetic snap collar designed to pair with most Tier 3–4 outerwear collars, or wear freestanding with the integrated neckwarmer band.

The crown is relaxed and slightly oversized, with two discreet horn-relief seams — widening gussets that accommodate small-to-medium geneware horns without distorting the silhouette. Ear panels are cut with extra depth for animal-ear geneware accommodation. Fully lined in smooth brushed fleece.
functionality: Magnetic snap collar attaches to compatible outerwear or worn standalone. Horn-relief gussets accommodate small-to-medium geneware horns. Deep ear panels fit standard and modified ear shapes. Water-shedding outer fiber layer.
what_it_says: You have enough taste to buy quality separates and enough sense to accommodate what your body has become.
worn_by: Tier 3 office workers who splurge on separates
story_hooks: A Halversen hood was found at a crime scene — the horn gussets were cut to an unusually large size, narrowing the suspect pool significantly.
Halversen's new Crofton supplier is a genemill with questionable labor practices; a Tier 3 buyer just found out and doesn't know what to do with that.
Someone is selling counterfeit Halversen hoods at Tier 2 markets — they look right but the magnetic snaps demagnetize in the rain.
